| [`AddTrackMenu.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/AddTrackMenu.tsx) | "Add Track" button and its instrument picker: a search field over every instrument by category. The picker floats (portalled to <body>) so nothing in the timeline can clip or cover it, and closes on an outside click or Escape. |
| [`ArrangeDialog.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/ArrangeDialog.tsx) | The Arrange a beat dialog: the producer arrangement tools in four tabs. Dark melody (a short seeded loop for trap, drill, rage or phonk), Drops & switches (drop-outs, stops, risers and reverse cymbals, beat switches, and speeding up into a drop: SpeedUpSection.tsx), Song form (a loop laid out as a whole song with section markers) and Producer tag (record or import it once, place it with one click). The store side is arrangeActions.ts; which tab is open lives in arrangeDialogStore.ts. |
| [`AudioClipEditor.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/AudioClipEditor.tsx) | The editor docked under the timeline for an audio clip (where the piano roll goes for note clips): its stretch of the sound with warp markers and gain envelope, gain and fades, Follow tempo (time-stretch), the sample's tempo and key, Tune, Chop sample. |
| [`AudioWarpGain.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/AudioWarpGain.tsx) | The warp markers and gain envelope drawn over the audio clip editor's waveform, and the pointer editing of both. |
| [`AutoBadge.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/AutoBadge.tsx) | "AUTO" next to a control an automation lane drives. Clicking it shows that lane on the timeline. |
| [`AutomationLane.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/AutomationLane.tsx) | The automation lane editor drawn over a track's lane in automation view: the envelope, its points and curves, and clicking, dragging and deleting them. |
| [`AutomationMenu.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/AutomationMenu.tsx) | The right-click menu of an automation lane: quick ramps over the loop region, clear, remove the lane. |
| [`BeatStoreDialog.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/BeatStoreDialog.tsx) | The beat-store export: one dialog that makes the package producers sell a beat with, as one .zip: a tagged MP3 preview (the producer tag laid over it at the start and/or every N seconds), the untagged WAV, the stems (track-outs), an optional cover image and a short info file, every file named with the tempo and key. Built on the same renders as the Export dialog (renderArrangement, renderStems), the tag pieces in beatPack.ts and the tag sound in producerTag.ts. |
| [`BuiltinPluginPanel.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/BuiltinPluginPanel.tsx) | The window of a built-in plugin (see builtinHost.ts): what it does, and a slider for each of its parameters with the value as the plugin shows it. Double-click a slider to put it back. Drawn into the plugin window (PluginWindow) through the plugin's createGui, like a WAM's own. |
| [`ChannelKitDialog.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/ChannelKitDialog.tsx) | The channel kit dialog: what the kit will hold (each piece and the bars it comes from), where its loudness goes, and the button that makes the .zip (audio/channelKit.ts renders it). |
| [`ChopSampleDialog.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/ChopSampleDialog.tsx) | Chop sample: cut a sample (an audio clip's part of its sound) into up to 16 chops, at its hits, into equal parts or by hand (drag, add and remove the markers on its waveform), hear each, and put them on a new Drum Rack track's pads with a clip that plays them: in a new order ("Chop and play", a seeded starting pattern) or as they were. Or onto a Slicer, as before. |
| [`ChordRiffBar.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/ChordRiffBar.tsx) | The piano roll's second toolbar for pitched clips: chords by scale degree (click I, V, vi, IV and the progression builds from the playhead, voiced smoothly), the arpeggiator (pattern, octaves, speed, note length) and the riff generator (a riff, lead line or bass line in the key that follows the chords on the other tracks; New riff gives another). The maths is in store/chordTools.ts; linked clips follow every change (see store/patterns.ts). |
| [`ClipContextMenu.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/ClipContextMenu.tsx) | The right-click menu for clips and empty lane space (edit, copy, duplicate, repeat, delete, new clip, insert pattern, paste, load audio, smart tools), and the menu items other menus share. |
| [`ClipView.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/ClipView.tsx) | One clip block on a track lane: its note marks or waveform, name, fades and crossfades, and the select / move / duplicate / trim / razor gestures (with snapping and edge auto-scroll). |
| [`CutToLengthDialog.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/CutToLengthDialog.tsx) | The Cut to length dialog: pick a length and the song is rebuilt from its sections to last that long (see cutToLength.ts). |
| [`DrumGroovePanel.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/DrumGroovePanel.tsx) | The piano roll's GROOVE panel for drum clips: a groove template in one click (straight, light or heavy swing on the hats, lazy, pushed), then each row's own swing, push or drag in time, velocity and off-beat velocity, so the hats swing while the kick and snare stay straight. The groove is the clip's (Clip.groove); the clip schedule plays it, live and in exports alike. |
| [`ExportDialog.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/ExportDialog.tsx) | The Export dialog: what to render (song, loop, stems, the intro plus loop for games, a video), its ending, format (WAV, MP3, Ogg, MP4), sample rate and bit depth, loudness normalizing, and the render with progress and cancel. |
| [`ExpressionLane.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/ExpressionLane.tsx) | The piano roll's controller lane under the notes. The clip's lanes: pitch bend, mod wheel (vibrato), sustain pedal, and any MIDI controller by number (CC lanes move the setting the controller is mapped to, and plugins get them as MIDI). And, with one note selected, that note's own bend and pressure (per-note expression). Curves: click to add a point, drag one to move it, right-click (or double-click) one to remove it; the lane glides between points. Sustain: drag along the lane to hold the pedal down there, click a held stretch to lift it. |
| [`FledgeSynthPanel.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/FledgeSynthPanel.tsx) | Fledge Synth's own window (the synth in engine/fledge-synth): its controls in sections across three tabs (Sound, Modulation, Effects), as a synth's panel lays them out, with the macros and presets always in view, a picture of each oscillator's wave, each LFO's shape, the envelopes, and an editor for the two drawn shapes. Knobs drag up and down (Shift for fine steps), take the arrow keys, and double-click back to where they started. Controls find their parameter by its name (see fledgeLayout.ts). |
| [`FolderRow.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/FolderRow.tsx) | A folder's row in the timeline: fold it away, rename and recolour it, mute or solo all its tracks, or ungroup it. The lane shows its tracks' clips in miniature, so a folded folder still shows where its music is. |
| [`FreezeButton.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/FreezeButton.tsx) | Freeze / unfreeze a track. Lit while its freeze plays; amber when the freeze is out of date (something it was rendered from changed, so the track plays live) and a click freezes it again. A faint ring marks a track auto-freeze is playing as audio (autoFreeze.ts). |
| [`GameCostumes.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/GameCostumes.tsx) | The Game tab's second tier: costumes (the song played other ways: each track on another instrument or silent, maybe faster; see costumes.ts) and how each state plays in the game (as written, or its pieces shuffled, with silences between plays). Heard in Audition like the game, shipped in the game kit. |
| [`GameMatrix.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/GameMatrix.tsx) | The Game preview's transition matrix (how each state hands over to each other one) and its audition pads (the states, rendered as the game will get them, played by the kit's own web player, so every crossfade, stinger bridge and intensity change sounds exactly as it will in the game). |
| [`GameParams.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/GameParams.tsx) | The Game tab's parameters: named values the game sets (danger, health, depth...), each moving several things in the music at once (see gameParams.ts). Heard with Audition, shipped in the game kit. |
| [`GamePreview.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/GamePreview.tsx) | The Game tab: hear the song the way a game will play it (sections as states switched on the beat, transitions, stingers, intensity, loop variations), and export the game kit, the web runtime kit and the FMOD / Wwise package. |
| [`IntensityPanel.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/IntensityPanel.tsx) | Intensity in the Game preview: the slider (the same one as in the header), each track's stem group and its on/off switch, and a curve per group in use: how loud its tracks play at each intensity. On a curve, drag a point to move it, click empty space to add one, double-click a point to remove it. A line marks the intensity now. |
| [`LaneFrameGrid.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/LaneFrameGrid.tsx) | Grid lines drawn across lanes for the visible stretch only: video frame lines while snapping to frames, and measure and beat lines in songs with other meters than 4/4. |
| [`LauncherPanel.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/LauncherPanel.tsx) | The Launcher tab: the clip launcher's grid (a column per track, a row per scene) with launch, stop and drag-to-move. The logic is launcher.ts. |
| [`LoopRangePopover.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/LoopRangePopover.tsx) | The exact loop range editor (In, Out and Length typed in bars or timecode), opened from the chevron beside the Loop button. |
| [`MarkerList.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/MarkerList.tsx) | The markers list popover (rename, lock to time or bar, delete, go to) and exporting the markers for video editing software. |
| [`Markers.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/Markers.tsx) | Markers on the timeline: their flags in the ruler (click to go there, drag to move, double-click to rename, right-click menu) and their lines across the lanes. |
| [`MicButton.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/MicButton.tsx) | The microphone record button: records the audio input onto an Audio track from the playhead, with punch in / out and loop takes. Bluetooth headphones (a slow output) are warned about as a take starts; a take going when the phone app goes to the background is stopped and kept. |
| [`MixerPanel.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/MixerPanel.tsx) | Every track side by side as a mixing-desk strip: a level meter, a fader, pan, the reverb and delay sends, mute and solo, and which inserts are on. The same settings as the track headers and the Inspector, so a change here is a change there (and one undo step per drag). |
| [`Modal.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/Modal.tsx) | A centred dialog over a dimmed page, closed by Esc, its close button or a click outside. |
| [`NewAudioTrackDrop.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/NewAudioTrackDrop.tsx) | The strip under the tracks: drop sound files here for a new Audio track at the dropped bar. |
| [`NotationView.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/NotationView.tsx) | A note clip as sheet music (drawn with VexFlow): a staff, or a grand staff when its notes span both, in the song's key and meter, with ties, beams and rests; drum clips on a percussion staff. The measure the playhead is in is lit. Export it as MusicXML for a notation program, or print it. |
| [`NoteRepeatPicker.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/NoteRepeatPicker.tsx) | The MIDI popover's NOTE REPEAT choice: off, or the rate a held drum pad repeats at (1/8 to 1/32 and their triplets), for finger drumming on a pad controller or the computer keyboard. |
| [`PianoRoll.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/PianoRoll.tsx) | The piano roll: the note editor for one note clip, docked under the timeline. Adding, moving, resizing and deleting notes, velocity, scales and chord stamps, the composing tools (noteTools.ts), drum and Slicer rows, the expression lane and the notation view switch, and how often the selected notes play (chance and step conditions: noteChance.ts). Positions are worked out in 96ths of a bar so notes never drift. |
| [`Playhead.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/Playhead.tsx) | The playhead: its line across the lanes and its handle in the ruler, and scrubbing it with the mouse. |
| [`PluginBrowser.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/PluginBrowser.tsx) | The built-in plugins (see audio/plugins/builtinHost.ts): search them, browse by category or collection, star favourites, and add one as an effect on a track (after its instrument, before its own inserts) or, for an instrument, as a new track. Its window opens once it's added. |
| [`PluginDialogs.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/PluginDialogs.tsx) | Web Audio Module plugins in the app: the dialog that adds one by URL (as a new Plugin track's instrument, or as an effect on a track), the floating window showing a plugin's own controls, and the bar asking before an opened project's plugins load. |
| [`ProjectBar.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/ProjectBar.tsx) | The project bar in the header: the song's name, Save, Export and Share, the autosave status, the New dialog (a blank timeline or a starter; opened from the File menu), and the banner offering to restore the last session. |
| [`RecordControls.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/RecordControls.tsx) | Recording and MIDI controls in the toolbar: the Record button and its settings (count-in, quantize, punch, takes, lining up microphone recording), the metronome, and the MIDI popover (devices, activity, the computer keyboard piano). |
| [`RollPainter.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/RollPainter.tsx) | The piano roll's ROLL painter: turns the selected notes (a hat note, or a long note drawn over a span) into a roll at 1/16, 1/16 triplet, 1/32, 1/32 triplet or 1/64, or a stutter of so many hits, with its velocity rising, falling or swelling and its pitch rising or falling as it goes (the drill hat roll). The notes themselves come from roll() in noteTools.ts; this is the panel. |
| [`RulerContextMenu.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/RulerContextMenu.tsx) | The ruler's right-click menu: add a marker, tempo or time-signature change there, insert or delete bars across every track, key changes, and speeding up into a drop (on the loop or the selected clips there). |
| [`SampleInfo.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/SampleInfo.tsx) | A sample's tempo and key as heard (sampleAnalysis.ts), with how sure, and the one-click matches: the song to the sample's tempo, or the sample (an audio clip) stretched to the song's tempo and moved into its key. Also the small badge an audio clip shows once its sound has been heard. |
| [`ShareDialog.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/ShareDialog.tsx) | The Share dialog: a link that opens the song (shareLink.ts), the mix as an MP3, or the project file with its sounds, handed to the device's share sheet where the browser has one and downloaded otherwise. |
| [`SmartDialog.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/SmartDialog.tsx) | The Chord progression and Drummer dialogs: make a clip from a few choices at the right-clicked bar (smartTools.ts writes the notes). |
| [`SpectrumView.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/SpectrumView.tsx) | The live master spectrum, drawn in one of the readout styles (spectrumSkins.ts): plain bars, or a character that moves to the sound. The style is remembered in this browser. |
| [`SpeedUpSection.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/SpeedUpSection.tsx) | The Arrange a beat dialog's "Speed up into the drop" section (Drops tab): pick a block of bars (the loop, the selected clips, or typed), how much of its end speeds up and by how much, the curve, and what happens on the drop; it shows the bars, beats and tempos before you press it. The store side is speedUpActions.ts; the maths is speedUp.ts. |
| [`StepLanes.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/StepLanes.tsx) | The piano roll's step lanes, under the notes (store/stepLanes.ts): a row of steps per lane on its own grid (1/16, 1/32, triplets, 1/8), each holding a value for one of the track's settings (a Fledge Synth macro, another of the plugin's parameters, the Filter's cutoff...). Drag across the steps to paint their heights; right-drag (or Alt-drag) to clear them (a cleared step holds the value before); the toolbar's tools randomise (seeded, within a range), repeat the first steps, shift them round and turn on "per note" (the value changes at each note in a set step). Each drag or tool is one undo step. |
| [`TakesDialog.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/TakesDialog.tsx) | A take folder's takes, one row each, with the comp: the lit stretch of each row is what plays. Drag along a row to have that take play there (snapped to beats; Shift for 16ths), or click a row's name to have it play throughout. Delete drops a take; Flatten keeps what the comp plays and drops the folder. |
| [`TempoRow.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/TempoRow.tsx) | The ruler's top row: the song's tempo and time signature, and their changes along the way. A faint line traces the tempo (glides show as slopes). Click a flag to edit it, drag one to move it (a tempo change snaps to the grid, a time signature to measure starts), double-click the row to add a tempo change there. The ruler's right-click menu adds either. |
| [`TimeRuler.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/TimeRuler.tsx) | The time ruler: bars and beats (or timecode), the tempo row, the loop In / Out brackets, marker flags, scrubbing and the playhead handle. |
| [`Timeline.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/Timeline.tsx) | The arrangement timeline: toolbar, ruler, the video lane, folder rows, sticky track headers and clip lanes, the playhead, marquee selection, zoom and scroll, keyboard shortcuts, and the editors docked under it (piano roll, audio clip editor). The heart of the UI. |
| [`TimelineResizer.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/TimelineResizer.tsx) | The bar under the timeline: drag it down to make the timeline taller (and push the panels under it down) to see more tracks at once, up to keep it compact. It stops at the last track: there's no empty space to drag into. Double-click fits every track in exactly (or, if it already does, goes back to the usual height). The height is kept in this browser. |
| [`TimelineScrollbar.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/TimelineScrollbar.tsx) | The overview scrollbar under the lanes: the whole song in miniature, with the visible window as a thumb to drag, click or stretch (zoom). |
| [`TimelineToolbar.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/TimelineToolbar.tsx) | The timeline's toolbar: transport (go to In, play, stop, loop and its exact range), record, metronome, Mic and MIDI, the position and timecode readouts, tools (select, razor), snap, undo / redo, the markers list, the Inspector toggle and zoom. |
| [`Toast.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/Toast.tsx) | The short message at the bottom of the screen (shown by showToast in toastStore.ts). Pocket shows it at the top instead, under the song's name, and lets touches through it, so it never covers the pads being played. |
| [`TrackHeader.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/TrackHeader.tsx) | A track's header on the left of its lane: name, colour, add clip, mute / solo / arm, volume and pan (or, in automation view, the lane picker, its value and MIDI learn), freeze, and selecting the track for the Inspector. |
| [`TrackLane.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/TrackLane.tsx) | A track's lane: its clips over the bar grid, double-click to make a clip, sound files dropped from the desktop (and pads from the retired sound deck: see dragSounds.ts), the right-click menu, and the automation lane in automation view. |
| [`TrackMenu.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/TrackMenu.tsx) | The right-click menu of a track header: colour, move, folders, buses, freeze / bounce (in place, or the loop range to a Drum Rack pad), delete. |
| [`TuneDialog.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/TuneDialog.tsx) | Tune a vocal (or any one-note-at-a-time recording): its pitch pulled onto the notes of a key. The graph shows the pitch sung (grey) and where it goes (colour) against the key's notes. Apply makes a tuned copy of the sound for the clip; the original is kept, and Untune goes back to it. Opened as Hard tune (or with that button) it starts at full strength and instant speed: the robotic sound (hardTune.ts). It's a processing step on the clip, so exports play the result. |
| [`VariationsDialog.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/VariationsDialog.tsx) | Generate variations: from one short clip, 4 to 8 takes for a game to pick from at random (footsteps, swings, clicks), each a little different in pitch, brightness, length and level. Save them as a .zip of WAVs, or lay them out on a new Audio track after the clip. |
| [`Waveform.tsx`](../src/components/timeline/Waveform.tsx) | Waveform drawings from a sound's precomputed peaks: a stretch of a sound (Waveform), and an audio clip's waveform laid along its warp markers (ClipWaveform). |
| [`arrangeDialogStore.ts`](../src/components/timeline/arrangeDialogStore.ts) | Which tab of the Arrange a beat dialog (ArrangeDialog.tsx) is open, and the bar and track it was opened for: kept outside the component so menus, the palette and right-click menus can open it. |
| [`audioFiles.ts`](../src/components/timeline/audioFiles.ts) | Sound files arriving on the timeline: dropped from the desktop onto an Audio track's lane or the space under the tracks, or picked with "Load audio…". Each goes into the sound library (see soundLibrary.ts) and becomes a clip. |
| [`automationHooks.ts`](../src/components/timeline/automationHooks.ts) | React hook for a control that follows an automation lane: the lane's value at the playhead, updated a few times a second while playing. |
| [`drawnStretch.ts`](../src/components/timeline/drawnStretch.ts) | Zoomed in, the timeline is up to 512,000 px wide, so the ruler labels and the lanes' frame lines are drawn only for the visible stretch plus at least this much either side. Scrolling redraws them once per chunk, not per frame. |
| [`gameKitSong.ts`](../src/components/timeline/gameKitSong.ts) | The song as the game kit needs it, from the store now. |
| [`layout.ts`](../src/components/timeline/layout.ts) | Shared timeline layout metrics (px). |
| [`menuHooks.ts`](../src/components/timeline/menuHooks.ts) | Close a popup menu on Esc, a click outside it, scrolling the page (or a panel) or resizing the window. |
| [`noteShades.ts`](../src/components/timeline/noteShades.ts) | A clip's note marks on the timeline as one SVG path per shade (velocity), instead of an element per note. |
| [`playheadReadout.ts`](../src/components/timeline/playheadReadout.ts) | The playhead for readouts (the position and timecode boxes, the overview's playhead): while playing, updated a few times a second on the shared frame loop; stopped, at once on every move. The store moves the playhead every frame, and a readout re-rendering with it changed text in the page's main layer every frame, which made the browser repaint the whole page (every clip and note on screen) sixty times a second during playback. Digits changing faster than this can't be read anyway; the playhead line itself still moves every frame (Playhead.tsx). |
| [`projectFile.ts`](../src/components/timeline/projectFile.ts) | Project files on disk. Where the browser lets a page write files (Chrome and Edge on a computer: the File System Access API), Save As asks where to save and what to call it, and from then on Save writes to that same file, as a desktop DAW does; Open uses the same picker, so Save updates the file that was opened. Elsewhere (Safari, Firefox, phones) Save downloads the file, to wherever the browser keeps downloads. |
| [`rows.ts`](../src/components/timeline/rows.ts) | The timeline's vertical layout: where each shown track's row starts, below the ruler, the video lane and the folder rows. |
| [`samplePackImport.ts`](../src/components/timeline/samplePackImport.ts) | Loading a sample pack: a folder of sound files, dropped or picked, sorted (see store/samplePack.ts) into Drum Rack kits, Multi Sampler instruments, an Audio track of its loops and pads for its other one-shots, each sound loaded into the library once. Says what it made, and what it left out and why. |
| [`stepTargets.ts`](../src/components/timeline/stepTargets.ts) | What a track's step lanes can move (store/stepLanes.ts), named for the menus of the studio's piano roll (StepLanes.tsx) and Pocket's roll: a Fledge Synth's macros by what they do ("Growl", "Grit"), the instrument plugin's other parameters by name, and the track's own settings (Filter cutoff and resonance, volume, pan, EQ, the inserts' settings). |
| [`toastStore.ts`](../src/components/timeline/toastStore.ts) | The toast's state: showToast puts a short message at the bottom of the screen. |

## src/native/

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`appLifecycle.ts`](../src/native/appLifecycle.ts) | The phone app going to the background and coming back, and the Back button (Capacitor's App plugin; nothing of this runs in a browser). |
| [`backButton.ts`](../src/native/backButton.ts) | The phone's Back button (Android): what it closes. Whatever is open over the screen registers how to close itself while it's open (a sheet, a dialog); the screens underneath register how to go back from where they are (Pocket's starters screen, the full piano roll). Back runs the newest that has something to do. With nothing left, the app goes to the background (appLifecycle.ts), as Home would, rather than closing and losing its place. |
| [`nativeApp.ts`](../src/native/nativeApp.ts) | Fledgetone as a phone app (Capacitor, see capacitor.config.json and docs/APP.md): the native pieces a web page can't have on a phone, behind plain functions the rest of the code calls. On the web each one does nothing (or answers false), so callers keep their browser way as well. |

## src/pocket/

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`PocketApp.tsx`](../src/pocket/PocketApp.tsx) | Pocket: Fledgetone on a phone, on one screen, after the studio: the song as a grid at the top (its sections and tracks: PocketGrid), the transport, and a drawer at the bottom that becomes the selected track's instrument (PocketDrawer). Turning the phone turns the grid into the studio's timeline, with the drawer beside it. What's done now and then opens over it (PocketSheets). It connects the song to the engine and the autosave as the studio's timeline does, so a song started here opens on a computer and back. |
| [`PocketDrawer.tsx`](../src/pocket/PocketDrawer.tsx) | Pocket's drawer: the bottom of the screen, in the selected track's colour, as that track's instrument for the selected section. Play (pads, the key's notes or chords), Draw (the drum steps or the piano roll), Sound (another instrument of its kind; a Drum Rack's Pads, what's on them) and Mix (its level, reverb, mute, solo); a vocal track sings instead. Mix all makes it a mixer for every track. Its handle makes it bigger or smaller (tap to step, or drag); the piano roll opens it full and puts it back. |
| [`PocketDrop.tsx`](../src/pocket/PocketDrop.tsx) | The Drop pad in Pocket's drawer: six big pads that do something to the whole mix for as long as a finger holds them (stutter, a filter sweep, tape stop, crush, gate, an echo throw: see effects/dropFx.ts). Several can be held at once; a pad pressed while the song is stopped plays it. While the song plays, a press starts on the next 16th and a let-go ends on one, so every move is in time. With Rec on while the section plays, each move is written into the Drop track's cell, from where it started to where it was let go, replacing what that effect had there; the song then plays it every time, in the studio and in exports too. Under the pads, the section's moves, with the playhead. |
| [`PocketGrid.tsx`](../src/pocket/PocketGrid.tsx) | Pocket's song grid: the whole song at once. In portrait the sections run down the page in song order and the tracks across (it reads like a lyric sheet); turned on its side in landscape it's the studio's timeline, sections left to right. Each cell shows what a track plays in a section; tapping one selects it for the drawer (and loops the section). A section's letter loops it, its ⋯ (or holding a letter) arranges the song; + adds a section (a copy of the selected one) or a track. Above it: Loop / Song (what Play plays), Mix all and + Track. |
| [`PocketMic.tsx`](../src/pocket/PocketMic.tsx) | Pocket and the microphone: the notice that Bluetooth headphones put takes late, and lining up recording on this phone (lineUpRun.ts: soft clicks played and recorded, to measure how late takes arrive). Asking for the microphone itself is useMicAsk.tsx. |
| [`PocketNotice.tsx`](../src/pocket/PocketNotice.tsx) | Pocket's opening notice: the phone version is in its early stages and the studio on a computer is the full experience. It shows each time Pocket opens until "Don't show this again" is ticked. Continue, or the phone's Back, closes it. |
| [`PocketPads.tsx`](../src/pocket/PocketPads.tsx) | The drawer's pads and steps, for the selected cell. Drum pads are laid out like an MPC (kick, snare, clap and hat along the bottom, under the thumb; a Drum Rack's pad 1 to 4 there, its empty pads opening the Pads tool to fill them); note pads are the song's key over six rows, low notes at the bottom; chord pads are the key's chords. With Rec on while the song plays the section, what's played is written into the cell on the nearest 16th. The drum steps show one drum at a time, a bar of 16ths as a block (a row per beat), so every step is a thumb wide; holding a lit step sets how often it plays (see noteChance.ts), and the dice roll the drum or the beat again in its style (smartTools.ts rollDrums). Blocks keep their size: a taller drawer shows more of them, and the rest scroll (useAnchoredScroll keeps the rows that matter in place as the drawer changes size). |
| [`PocketRack.tsx`](../src/pocket/PocketRack.tsx) | The Pads tool of a Drum Rack track ("Your pads") in Pocket's drawer: its 16 pads, the chosen one's level and pitch, and ways to fill it: bounce the selected section onto it (the whole mix or one track), or a vocal take. The work is in bounceToPadActions.ts (and pocketBounce.ts). |
| [`PocketRoll.tsx`](../src/pocket/PocketRoll.tsx) | Pocket's piano roll (Draw, for keys, bass and synths): the selected cell's notes on rows of the song's key (and any other notes it has), over the instrument's range, a column per 16th. Both are a fixed size and the roll scrolls. One finger draws (tap for a note as long as the pen, drag right to make it longer), moves a note (drag it) or stretches it (drag its right end); two fingers scroll, as do the note names and the ruler; dragging to an edge scrolls that way. Pens: Note, Chord (a chord in the key in one tap) and Erase. Tapping a note selects it, and the bar above edits it in steps (and sets how often it plays: noteChance.ts). A gesture works on a draft and saves once, as one undo step, when it ends. |
| [`PocketShare.tsx`](../src/pocket/PocketShare.tsx) | Pocket's Share screen: the song as an MP3 (handed to the phone's share sheet where it has one, else downloaded), a link that opens the song (in Pocket on a phone, in the studio on a computer), the project file to save or open, and the switch to the full studio. |
| [`PocketSheets.tsx`](../src/pocket/PocketSheets.tsx) | What opens over Pocket's one screen, for the things done now and then: the song (its name, tempo, key, metronome, a new song, the file), sharing it, adding an instrument (or your own pads), arranging the song from a section (repeat it, make it its own, move it, a build-up, bounce it to a pad, take it out), a chord progression for the piano roll, the song's earlier versions, and the starters screen ("What are we making?"). |
| [`PocketSteps.tsx`](../src/pocket/PocketSteps.tsx) | Pocket's step lane, pinned under its piano roll: one lane at a time, for one of the track's Fledge Synth macros (the Filter's cutoff on other instruments), a column per step lined up with the roll's 16ths. Drag a finger across the steps to set their heights; with the Erase pen it clears them (a cleared step holds the value before). The name at the left picks the macro shown. Each drag is one undo step. The studio's piano roll has every target, grid and tool (store/stepLanes.ts). |
| [`PocketSynth.tsx`](../src/pocket/PocketSynth.tsx) | Pocket's Sound tool for a Fledge Synth track (the app's own synth): its presets by category, the preset's macros as big sliders under their plain names (Growl, Grit, Squelch...), the wobble's rate in time with the song (1/1 to 1/32, triplets too) when the sound has one, and the sound as a file to send (Share this sound, Open a sound file). Every move is an undo step, as a turn of the studio panel's knobs is (pluginEdits.ts). Other instruments are a tap away. |
| [`PocketVocals.tsx`](../src/pocket/PocketVocals.tsx) | Pocket's Vocals screen: sing over the song. One big button records from the phone's microphone while the song plays (from the loop's start when the loop is on, stopping by itself at its end; else from the playhead until tapped again), and the take lands on a vocal track where it was sung. Each vocal track wears one of the vocal chains (clean lead, aggressive, ad-lib...); each take can be doubled, hard-tuned (the studio's Tune dialog), put on a pad (whole, or chopped at its hits onto a new Drum Rack's pads) or deleted. In the drawer it's the selected vocal track's (`trackId`), and the transport's Rec starts and stops it (singRequest). The microphone is asked for properly (useMicAsk.tsx), recording can be lined up on the phone, and a take going when the app goes to the background is stopped and kept (holdTake). |
| [`pocketBounce.ts`](../src/pocket/pocketBounce.ts) | Pocket's "bounce a section to a pad": the section (everything playing, or one track) rendered onto a Drum Rack pad (see bounceToPadActions.ts), with what it says as it goes, and the drawer then showing that pad. Used by the section sheet and the Pads tool. |
| [`pocketCell.ts`](../src/pocket/pocketCell.ts) | The cell Pocket's drawer edits: the selected track in the selected section. Its notes are read relative to the section's start (from whatever clips are there), and the first edit makes the cell one clip spanning the section (pocketSections.cellClip), so every edit after is a plain change of that clip's notes. Also the hooks the screens share: the song's sections, the selected track and section, and the key. |
| [`pocketExport.ts`](../src/pocket/pocketExport.ts) | Pocket's one export: the whole song as an MP3 at the streaming loudness (the studio's Export dialog with its defaults: the song from bar 1, ringing out, matched to the default loudness target, peaks held under the lossy ceiling). Uses the same render as the studio, so the file sounds the same whichever made it. |
| [`pocketGrid.ts`](../src/pocket/pocketGrid.ts) | Pocket's note maths, as plain functions: how many 16th steps a bar has, how many steps a note covers, note names to MIDI numbers and back, and the notes of the song's key over an instrument's range (the rows of the pads and the piano roll). |
| [`pocketMode.ts`](../src/pocket/pocketMode.ts) | Which interface opens: Pocket (the phone version, src/pocket/) or the full studio. Phones get Pocket unless the person chose the studio; `?pocket` or `?studio` in the address picks one and remembers it (so a computer can try Pocket too). The same song plays in both: they share the store, the engine and the autosave. |
| [`pocketSections.ts`](../src/pocket/pocketSections.ts) | Pocket's song as sections: the stretches between the song's bar markers (or every 4 or 8 bars when it has none, as the studio's Cut to length reads them), each lettered by what's in it, so two sections playing the same thing share a letter (A A B A). A cell of Pocket's grid is one track in one section, edited as one clip spanning the section (cellClip makes it so). |
| [`pocketSession.ts`](../src/pocket/pocketSession.ts) | Pocket's care for the phone it runs on: the last song opens again by itself (a phone reloads a page it put away more often than a computer does), the screen stays awake while the song plays, a light buzz answers a pad where the phone can, and Play plays what Pocket shows. |
| [`pocketSound.ts`](../src/pocket/pocketSound.ts) | What Pocket's pads and grids play: the drum kit's sounds in pad order (or a Drum Rack's own 16 pads), and audition (a note through a track as it sounds in the song, starting the audio on the first tap). |
| [`pocketStore.ts`](../src/pocket/pocketStore.ts) | Pocket's own view state, apart from the song (useTimelineStore): which track and section are selected (the drawer edits that cell), which of its tools the drawer shows and how tall it is, the mixer, Rec, the open sheet and the key the note editors use. Plus the helpers its screens share: which editor a track opens in, the playhead while playing, and the drummer style each cell was last written in (the dice roll in it). |
| [`pocketUi.tsx`](../src/pocket/pocketUi.tsx) | Pocket's small shared pieces: a bottom sheet (a list that slides up over the screen), a card section, the button style, sized for thumbs (at least 44 px), and the chooser of how often a note plays. |
| [`useMicAsk.tsx`](../src/pocket/useMicAsk.tsx) | Asking for the microphone in Pocket: in the phone app, the first time, a plain word about why before the phone's own question; when it's refused, how to allow it, with a way to the app's settings on Android (or the site's settings in a browser), and Try again. |

## src/pwa/

Fledgetone as an installed app: the service worker (sw.js, filled in by the production build), its registration and updates, the install prompt and instructions.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`installAdvice.ts`](../src/pwa/installAdvice.ts) | How to install Fledgetone as an app in a browser that doesn't offer the install prompt to the page (Safari, Firefox, or Chrome and Edge when they've decided not to): a short sentence by browser and system. Plain logic on the user agent string, so Node tests it. |
| [`pwa.ts`](../src/pwa/pwa.ts) | Fledgetone as an installed app: registers the service worker (src/pwa/sw.js, production builds on fledgetone.com only), tells when a new version is ready (the page moves to it only when the person clicks Reload, after writing the autosave, and then opens What's new at its entries), offers the browser's install prompt, and asks the browser to keep this site's storage (the autosave, the library and the recordings) when the disk runs low. |
| [`sw.js`](../src/pwa/sw.js) | The service worker (served as /sw.js by the production build only: vite.config.ts fills in the build's id, the files to keep and the font stylesheets). It keeps the app itself (the page, its scripts and styles, the icons and the fonts) so the app opens at once, and offline, after one visit, and a new version downloads only the files that changed. |
